Character-specific appends suppress matching table commands rather than positively selecting executable attacks.
AppendCharacterAttackExclusions accurately names the producer and corrects the misleading rendered list-builder interpretation.
The declaration gives s32[8] and a u8 count; the builder does not reset the count and can dereference the cached target in Kirby's scale branch.
Subsequent table selection skips entries matching the appended commands, establishing the corrected purpose.
Checked all character ranges, command constants, capacity guards, airborne exceptions and Kirby numeric comparisons against the canonical switch.
Inclusive remainder thresholds yield the stated fractions; 121/240 exceeds 121/300, disproving monotonic veto reduction.
The relevant comparison reads x34_scale.y, not cur_pos.y; the surrounding contextual selection paths agree.
Controller branches preserve the distinct counters and cached-command outcomes. The interpreter's Done case clears command state without cancelling fighter motion.
The Yoshi continuation reads positions and island records, writes CPU tracking state on failure, and appends commands in every branch.
Reset arithmetic and the decrement/reject consumer establish an integer ranged/item decision cooldown.
CpuFighter.x34 is explicitly int, so assignment conversion precedes optional integer division.
Held-item decision paths write xA4 before true returns, and the canonical item enum identifies M_Ball as Poke Ball.
The caller supplies GET_ITEM(fp->item_gobj); SelectHeldItemAction distinguishes this routine from the tracked-item table selector.
The ordered timer, ammunition, angular, facing and distance branches match; the Poke Ball exception corrects the Metal Box misidentification.
The predicate accepts only GuardOn and Guard. GuardSetOff setup installs hitlag callbacks and response behavior, while GuardOff has a distinct transition.
HSD_Randf is inside the nonzero-delay guard, so level 9 consumes no sample. Interpreter reads confirm R persists across Done.
The builder emits downward-stick B outside its numeric motion guard, and selector 3 reaches it from grounded as well as eligible airborne paths.
The endpoint helper returns -1 on failure, but the caller compares against a runtime doubled threshold. Deferring the threshold sign avoids an unsupported unconditional reversal claim.
The defensive dispatcher and helpers match the stated cached inputs and command outputs; FireBlaster literally emits downward-stick B.
Behavior-7 dispatch and the defensive decision tree support reaction-command construction, not a blaster interpretation inferred from the helper name.
Checked selector-zero cleanup, dodge guards, character exceptions, grounded item-pointer precondition, random split and the strict 30-unit boundary.

contradictions.reason: Accepted deferral of all nine compiled-section facts. The source contains local types and a conditional literal-order helper, not compiled evidence establishing section objects, extent, alignment or ordering.
The two rendered name collisions are resolved by supported distinctions: tracked-item attack versus held-item action, and grounded jump policy versus its mode-16 alternate.

The aerial-pursuit height claim was reversed; the proposal correctly preserves the higher-target continuation and null-target double terminator. Accepted deferral of the external jump-subtype transfer link: the query and state-8 execution are established, but the exact transfer site remains unexamined.

All six exclusion-builder corrections are supported: these are bounded s32 exclusions, not bytecode or chosen attacks. Accepted deferral of both affected link explanations because link replacement is outside scope. Kirby's union spelling remains insufficient to assign panic-charge semantics.
The veto duty fraction is not monotonic, and the main selector's size comparison concerns vertical scale rather than positional height. Both factual corrections are supported.
Done ends interpretation rather than the attacking motion; Yoshi continuation does not mutate fighter positions. The proposal correctly separates command construction from gameplay motion.
The previously uncertain cooldown role is established by its consumer, and its field is int rather than floating-point. Both cooldown corrections are supported.
Both held-item explanations correctly replace Metal Box with Poke Ball; the canonical enum distinguishes those item kinds.
GuardSetOff is not shield release, and Guard at level 9 draws no RNG. Accepted deferral of the shielding link's incorrect release explanation because links cannot be replaced in this proposal.
Accepted the literal runtime-threshold formulation and deferral of its sign. Endpoint failure alone cannot establish unconditional reversal.

The down-special builder has a grounded call path. All three defensive-dispatch corrections appropriately replace the unsupported blaster interpretation with the actual downward-stick B stream while preserving exceptional branches and cached-pointer preconditions.
